archetype.name: Dual-Threat (power runner, vertical passer)
archetype.definition: A big-armed passer who takes more downfield shots than he used to, extends plays into high-value scrambles, and serves as his own goal-line back.

report.headline: The deep ball is carrying him; the rushing touchdowns won't keep this pace.
report.take:
Allen is in his ninth season and still plays the way he always has. He pushes the ball downfield, uses his legs as a second offense, and accepts some turnovers as the cost. What has changed in 2026 is the mix. He's completing fewer passes than last year (66.1% against 69.3%) but gaining more per attempt (8.59 YPA, up 0.62), because he's throwing deeper and more often into tight windows. His aggressiveness is up 1.8 points, and his intended air yards (8.85) are well above the 7.1 aDOT he ran in 2025. That YPA ranks 5th among 49 qualifiers, and his 0.234 EPA per dropback sits nearly a quarter-point above the league average.

The engine is the vertical game. On 36 throws of 20+ air yards he has added 0.739 EPA a play with a 9.6 CPOE and six touchdowns. Anything 10+ yards downfield has produced 9 of his 12 TD passes. He also has a spread of reliable targets: Shakir, Kincaid and Coleman are all near half a point of EPA per target. The one outlier is DJ Moore at 0.142 on 32 looks. The offense ranks 3rd in EPA even though it leans run-heavy, passing 4.8 points less than expected (25th). Allen's volume is modest, and his efficiency is doing the work.

The surface numbers hide two things. First, his fantasy line (25.1 PPR a game, 1st) is propped up by 9 rushing touchdowns, 7 of them on designed runs that average just 2.66 yards a carry. He's a short-yardage plunger near the goal line. That's a real role, but the TD count is a small-sample spike on top of it. It also explains why his red-zone passing looks ugly (-0.056 EPA, -9.9 CPOE): the easy scores go on the ground. Second, the deep-ball success has a cost. Four of his six interceptions came on those 20+ throws, and his INT rate ranks 31st. That fits a career in which he's routinely been near the bottom of the league in picks.

The last three games have cooled. EPA per dropback is down 0.073 from his season mark and rushing yards are down 20.3 a game. That stretch ended with a sack-heavy grind against Minnesota, the league's top defense, likely without left tackle Dion Dawkins. He's still clearly above average as a passer, but the 35-40 point ceiling from September depended on rushing touchdowns that were never going to keep coming at that rate.

strengths.title: Downfield accuracy driving efficiency
strengths.body: His 20+ yard throws are producing 0.739 EPA a play with a 9.6 CPOE, and the 10-19 range is strong too at 0.394. It's a deliberate shift: he's more aggressive and throwing deeper than his conservative 2025, and he's being rewarded with a top-5 YPA. The rate on 36 deep attempts will drift down, but the arm and the willingness are career traits.

strengths.title: Scrambles as a drive-saver
strengths.body: Twenty scrambles have gone for 209 yards and 13 first downs at 1.117 EPA apiece. That is the payoff for holding the ball 2.89 seconds. It also explains a middling pressure-to-sack rate (28.9%), which is a big improvement on last year's 40.4%. This has been part of his game for nine seasons and should hold.

strengths.title: Steady under late, close pressure
strengths.body: In one-score fourth quarters he's at 0.421 EPA a play with a 6.5 CPOE, and on third downs he carries an 8.1 CPOE while facing an average of 8 yards to go. In the moments that decide close games, his accuracy goes up rather than down.

concerns.title: Rushing touchdowns are running hot
concerns.body: Nine rushing scores, seven on designed runs averaging 2.66 yards with a 21.9% stuff rate, means the touchdowns are coming from goal-line usage, not explosive running. The role is stable, but the count will slow. He has gone without a rushing score in two of the last three games, and his fantasy output has dropped with it.

concerns.title: Interceptions are the cost of aggression
concerns.body: Six picks rank 31st in INT rate, and five came on throws of 10+ air yards. Add four turnover-worthy fumbles, too. This is the price of the deep-ball approach, and his career says it isn't a fluke: he has had seasons of 15 and 18 picks. Expect a steady trickle, not a fix.

concerns.title: Protection without Dawkins
concerns.body: Dion Dawkins (99% of snaps) is listed out with a rib injury. Allen took 4 sacks against Minnesota, and 8 of his 17 sacks have come on third down. If Dawkins sits again, longer-developing deep shots become harder to set up.

trend.note: His passing efficiency has eased from a torrid start (0.161 EPA per dropback over the last three, against 0.234 for the season) and his rushing has dried up lately. The Week 9 dud came against the league's best defense, so this is a cooling from a high level, not a collapse.

nextGame.headline: A leaky Jets pass defense and a big spread favor Allen
nextGame.body:
The Jets rank 30th in pass EPA allowed and 31st against short throws, so Allen's high-volume short game (0.254 EPA on 0-9 yard throws) should stay on schedule. Their stinginess in QB yards allowed (227.6, 4th) doesn't match a defense that gives up 2 passing TDs a game (26th), so the efficiency should translate into scoring. Their real strength is taking away WR1s (-5.4 PPR under average, 2nd). That points the volume toward Kincaid and the secondary wideouts: tight ends get 0.39 EPA a target against them (25th), and WR2s 0.42 (26th). Their 10th-ranked sack rate is the threat, especially with Buffalo's line in question.

Availability matters on both sides. Dawkins is listed out for Buffalo, which puts a dent in the protection Allen needs for his deep shots. For New York, edge Joseph Ossai is out, which softens that pass rush somewhat. Garrett Wilson is also out, which weakens the Jets' offense. With Buffalo favored by 8.5 (-550 moneyline), the main risk is a comfortable lead that hands the game to a run-leaning offense and trims Allen's attempts.

keyMatchups.title: Short game against a soft underneath
keyMatchups.body: The Jets allow 0.246 EPA on short passes, 31st in the league, and their success-rate defense ranks 30th. Allen's 0-9 yard throws already run a 50.5% success rate. Expect a long run of chain-moving completions to Shakir and Kincaid.

keyMatchups.title: Kincaid against a weak TE defense
keyMatchups.body: Kincaid leads Allen's top targets at 0.526 EPA a target. The Jets have let lead tight ends beat their averages and allow 0.39 EPA a target to them, both bottom-eight marks. With the Jets' WR1 coverage strong, the middle of the field is the obvious place to attack.

keyMatchups.title: Jets pass rush against a patched line
keyMatchups.body: New York's sack rate ranks 10th, and Buffalo may be without Dawkins again after four sacks in Week 9. Ossai's absence helps. Allen's quicker 2.64-2.74 second release over the last two games suggests the staff is already adjusting.

nextGame.watch: Whether Dawkins plays, and whether Buffalo still takes deep shots if he doesn't.

restOfSeason.body:
The passing core is sustainable: an aggressive, accurate downfield passer in a top-3 offense with three productive targets. His deep-ball EPA will come down from 0.739 as the sample grows, so expect his YPA to settle closer to his last-five 8.27 than his season 8.59. Expect efficiency to stay top-10 but volume to stay capped by a run-leaning, frequently leading team. Somewhere around 240-265 passing yards is the likely band.

The rushing is where regression comes. The goal-line role is real, but a ~2.7-yard designed-run average won't keep producing touchdowns at this pace, and his recent rushing yardage has slipped. Figure on roughly one rushing score every two or three games and 25-40 rushing yards. That puts his fantasy output in the high teens to mid-20s rather than the 25+ he has averaged. Interceptions will keep coming at around three every four games, because they're part of the deep-ball approach.
swingFactors: Dawkins' health and the pass protection
Whether the goal-line rushing role holds
Game script as a heavy favorite capping attempts

confidence.note: Eight games, a deep-ball split on 36 throws, and a rushing-TD spike; the career baseline is stable.
